OmaStats 1.6.1 keeps the sampler running whatever another process is named, and keeps an IP address you copy out of sight of other users on the machine.

[Download the complete plugin](https://github.com/crmne/omastats/releases/download/v1.6.1/omastats-v1.6.1.tar.gz), or install it with:

```sh
omarchy plugin add https://github.com/crmne/omastats.git --enable
```

## Fixed

- **A process name can no longer stop the sampler.** When a process name fills the kernel's 15 bytes, OmaStats compares it with the program's file name to show the full one, and it cut the name at byte 8 to do so. If a character of two or more bytes, such as "é", crossed that byte, the sampler crashed, and it crashed again on every restart for as long as that process ran, leaving the panel without figures. Any local user could name a process that way. The names are now compared byte by byte. By @crmne; thanks @HANCORE-linux (omacom/omarchy-plugin-marketplace#11213).
- **Copied addresses stay private.** Clicking an IP address on the Network page passed it to `wl-copy` on its command line, and `wl-copy` keeps running until you copy something else, so every user on the machine could read the address in its process arguments. It now goes to `wl-copy` on its standard input. By @crmne.

## Known limitations

- The process search and color fields take typed text only: there is no paste or text selection.
- GPU process lists from open drivers show only your own processes. An integrated AMD card's own load figure jumps between 0% and 100%, so it can disagree with its process list.
- CPU power on Intel, and on AMD without integrated graphics, needs a udev rule that makes `/sys/class/powercap/*/energy_uj` readable.
- Version 1.4.1 and earlier can't read a disk saved by id. If you go back to an older version, choose the disk again in Settings.
- A mirror, raidz or striped ZFS pool counts against its first data drive only. "All disks" is correct, but picking another drive in the pool shows no space for it.
- A vertical bar with many readouts turned on can run into the bar's center section. Turn off readouts you don't need, or use figure-only looks.

## Thanks

Thanks @HANCORE-linux for finding the process-name crash during the marketplace review.

Both bundled binaries are rebuilt twice in CI, compared byte-for-byte with the committed executables, and covered by checksums and GitHub build attestations.
